_meta.source: Hand-transcribed from CS_CE_Career_Guide_2027.md v2.0: §10.1 (scores D1–D6), §10.3 (comp bands), §10.4 (majors), §10.5 (scenario grades), profile sections §3–5 (summary, anchors). If the guide changes, update this file and rebuild.

D1.name: Demand durability
D1.desc: Will there be many jobs in 2031–2045?

D2.name: AI resistance
D2.desc: Does AI complement (5) or substitute (1) the work?

D3.name: Moat
D3.desc: Barrier to entry: hardware, physics, clearance, regulation, deep math.

D4.name: Compensation
D4.desc: Pay trajectory relative to other computing careers.

D5.name: Optionality
D5.desc: How easily you can move to other fields later.

D6.name: BS-accessible
D6.desc: Reachable with a bachelor's, without MS/PhD.

careers.name: Infrastructure / Distributed Systems / Platform (incl. AI infra, SRE)
careers.summary: The picks and shovels of AI: GPU clusters, inference serving, storage, networking, observability. The only Tier 1 field that is simultaneously BS-accessible, high-optionality, and AI-resistant — the safest single bet.
careers.degree_note: Either. OS, distributed systems, networks; Rust/Go; cloud + Kubernetes.
careers.sensitivity: Low: grows in A and B; holds in C
avoid_if: You want visible, user-facing products
You dislike on-call and operations

careers.name: Security Engineer (cloud, AppSec, AI security, detection & response)
careers.summary: BLS +29% growth; AI both attacks and defends; counter-cyclical demand; a citizenship moat in government and defense. The most BS-accessible Tier 1 field.
careers.degree_note: OS, networks, crypto; CTF team; Security+ if defense-bound.
avoid_if: You want to build products rather than protect them

careers.name: Robotics / Embedded / Autonomy ("Physical AI")
careers.summary: Humanoids, drones, autonomous vehicles, defense systems. Needs hardware + software + ML at once — a rare combination that AI cannot yet replace because the work touches the physical world.
careers.degree_note: Controls, signals, embedded systems, ROS 2; robotics team.
careers.grad_school: Helpful for perception/planning; not needed for embedded
avoid_if: You want remote work
You dislike debugging hardware

careers.name: Semiconductor / Chip Design, Verification & Architecture
careers.summary: Highest median pay of any computing occupation ($155k BLS); acute talent shortage (~67k unfilled by 2030); CHIPS Act fabs and the AI accelerator race. The best moat in computing; DV/FPGA/test are BS-accessible.
careers.degree_note: VLSI, computer architecture, digital verification; Tiny Tapeout; plan an MS for design/architecture.
careers.sensitivity: Low: strong in A, B, C
careers.grad_school: MS recommended for design/architecture; not for DV/FPGA
avoid_if: You want to change fields easily later
You dislike EE coursework

careers.name: AI / Machine Learning Engineer (applied)
careers.summary: Fastest-growing, highest-paid engineering discipline (openings +60% YoY; median MLE comp ~$279k). Lowest moat in Tier 1 and the most crowded — the best bet for students who can stand out.
careers.degree_note: Math or statistics minor; ML systems / GPU programming; undergrad research.
careers.sensitivity: Medium: highest upside in B, compresses in C
careers.grad_school: MS raises odds at labs; not required for product-company MLE
avoid_if: You dislike math and probabilistic systems
You want low competition

careers.name: Data Engineer / Engineering-heavy Data Scientist
careers.summary: BLS +34% growth for data scientists; every AI system is a data pipeline. Tier 1 with a caveat: the analyst/dashboard layer is automating; the platform and engineering layer is growing.
careers.degree_note: Databases, statistics; SQL depth; one warehouse; orchestration.
careers.sensitivity: Medium: analyst layer erodes; platform layer grows
careers.grad_school: MS in stats/DS common but not required
avoid_if: You want to stay on the analyst/BI side

careers.name: Defense, Aerospace & National-Security Engineering (cleared)
careers.summary: Clearance = citizen-only moat; neo-primes (Anduril, SpaceX, Palantir) hiring intensely; budget-driven and counter-cyclical. Scores 26.5 — Tier 1 for US citizens; Tier 2 only because of the citizenship gate.
careers.degree_note: US citizenship; clearance-track internships; SMART/SFS; embedded or infra depth.
avoid_if: You are not a US citizen
You want remote work or startup pace

careers.name: Energy, Climate & Grid Technology Computing
careers.summary: Data-center power demand is structural; grid software, power electronics, and controls are under-supplied and unfashionable. Mission with a tailwind; utility-scale pay is the drawback.
careers.degree_note: Power systems, control, embedded; energy economics.
careers.sensitivity: Low: data-center power demand is structural
avoid_if: Top-of-market comp is your priority

careers.name: Fintech, Quantitative Development & Trading Technology
careers.summary: The highest new-grad pay in computing ($200–350k at HFT firms) behind brutal selection; fintech more broadly is cyclical but large. For elite algorithmic/math talent.
careers.degree_note: Math double; probability, stochastic processes, C++; ICPC/Putnam.
careers.sensitivity: Medium: quant is elite-only; fintech cyclical
careers.grad_school: Not needed for quant dev; PhD common for quant research
avoid_if: You want work-life balance
You are not in the top few percent at competitive programming/math

careers.name: Forward Deployed Engineer / AI Solutions Engineer
careers.summary: Postings +800–1,100% in a year; TC $350–550k at AI labs; engineering plus customer-facing judgment in messy organizations — structurally AI-resistant. A bet on enterprise AI adoption.
careers.degree_note: Communication courses; a business or domain minor; hackathons.
careers.sensitivity: High: a bet on enterprise AI adoption (A/B)
avoid_if: You dislike travel and customer pressure
You want deep technical specialization

careers.name: Quantum Computing Engineer
careers.summary: Tiny field (~16.5k globally) with heavy capital inflow; long-dated bet independent of the AI cycle. For physics-minded CE students who plan on grad school.
careers.degree_note: Quantum mechanics, linear algebra, information theory; plan PhD/MS.
avoid_if: You want a job straight from a BS
You want a large, liquid job market

careers.name: Healthcare, Biotech & Life-Sciences Computing
careers.summary: Aging population + AI drug discovery + regulated (slow to automate) + FDA moat. Demographics-driven and robust in every scenario; slower pay growth.
careers.degree: CS (+ bio) or CE for devices
careers.degree_note: Biology/statistics minor; HIPAA/FDA literacy; research lab.
avoid_if: Top-of-market comp is your priority
You dislike regulated, slower-moving environments

careers.name: General Software Engineering at Top-Tier Employers
careers.summary: The largest market by far and a fine first job — if you enter through a specialized team (infra, security, ML platform, payments) and acquire a Tier 1 moat within two years. Weakest moat; hardest entry ramp.
careers.degree_note: Systems depth; two internships; enter via a specialized team.
careers.sensitivity: High: Scenario B hits generalists hardest
avoid_if: You plan to stay a generalist
You want low competition

careers.name: Technical Product Management (after engineering years)
careers.summary: A year-5 pivot for engineers with judgment, not a new-grad target. AI-resistant because the work is deciding what to build and why.
careers.degree_note: Ship as an engineer first; writing; business minor optional.
careers.sensitivity: Low, but not a first job
avoid_if: You want a new-grad role in it
You want to stay hands-on technical

careers.name: Graphics, Game Engines, Simulation & Spatial Computing
careers.summary: Math-heavy visual engineering: rendering, engines, physics simulation, robotics sim, AR/VR. Strong moat; avoid the game-studio treadmill and build engines/tools instead.
careers.degree_note: Linear algebra, computer graphics, GPU programming, physics.
avoid_if: You want a large job market
You want to make games at a studio (see 5.5)

careers.name: Developer Tools (engineering track)
careers.summary: Compilers, languages, build systems, IDEs, AI coding tools. Tool builders with compilers/PL/systems depth are scarce; the AI-coding-tools boom raised demand.
careers.degree_note: Compilers, PL, systems; open-source maintainer track.
avoid_if: You dislike abstract systems work

careers.name: Cloud / DevOps / Platform at Non-Tech Enterprises
careers.summary: Steady, unglamorous, everywhere: banks, retailers, hospitals, insurers all run cloud platforms. Flexibility, balance, and non-coastal living; a lower ceiling.
careers.degree_note: Cloud certs (professional level), Terraform, Kubernetes.
avoid_if: Top-of-market comp is your priority

careers.name: Developer Relations / Technical Education
careers.summary: For engineers who love teaching and writing. Funded from marketing budgets, so volatile; best as a later move from an engineering role.
careers.degree_note: Engineering depth first; writing and speaking; open-source visibility.
avoid_if: You want stability
You want a first job in it

careers.name: Contrarian Niches (COBOL/mainframe, analog/RF, OT/PLC, medical firmware, formal methods, PQC, EDA, HPC)
careers.summary: Where talent is fleeing and demand is not: mainframe modernization, analog/RF, industrial controls, medical firmware, formal verification, post-quantum crypto, EDA tools, HPC. Out-scores most of Tier 2; Tier 3 only because each niche is small.
careers.degree_note: Whatever the niche demands (COBOL, FPGA, controls, HPC/Fortran+MPI, SAT/SMT).
avoid_if: You want a large, liquid job market or prestige

careers.name: Research Scientist / Academia (PhD path)
careers.summary: Five to six more years for a shot at industrial research labs or the professoriate. Enormous moat and optionality, but a long, underpaid road and a funding-climate dependency.
careers.degree_note: Undergraduate research from year 2; publications; NSF GRFP.
avoid_if: You want to earn a full salary before ~2036

careers.name: Computing + Medicine (MD/DO path)
careers.summary: Physician-engineers are rare and valuable (clinical AI, informatics, medical devices) but the path is 11+ years and the CS degree is a complement, not the career.
careers.degree_note: Pre-med requirements alongside CS; clinical informatics exposure.
avoid_if: You are not committed to medicine itself

careers.name: Computing + Law / Policy / Government
careers.summary: AI regulation, privacy, IP, and technology policy need people who understand both code and institutions. Usually requires a JD or a policy master's; a niche, not a mass market.
careers.degree_note: Writing-heavy electives; policy or economics minor; JD or MPP later.
avoid_if: You want to stay hands-on technical

careers.name: Generalist Web / Full-Stack Developer
careers.summary: The most AI-exposed engineering role; frontend-only titles are disappearing fastest. Learn it as a foundation — it is not a destination.
careers.degree_note: Fine as a skill; pair with systems depth or a Tier 1 specialty.
careers.sensitivity: Very high: the most AI-exposed engineering role
avoid_if: You want a durable career identity

careers.name: Teaching CS (K-12 / community college)
careers.summary: Chronically under-supplied and meaningful, but poorly paid relative to every other option here. Best as a mission choice with eyes open.
careers.degree_note: Education minor or certification; tutoring/TA experience.
avoid_if: Compensation matters to you

careers.name: Native Mobile Development (iOS / Android)
careers.summary: Cross-platform frameworks and AI compress it; a declining specialty. Useful skill, weak career identity.
careers.degree_note: Pair with systems, ML-on-device, or security.
avoid_if: You want a durable career identity

careers.name: Game Development (studios)
careers.summary: Layoffs, crunch, and low pay for the passion premium. If you love games, build engines, graphics, or simulation (4.9) instead.
careers.degree_note: Graphics, engines, networking; ship a game as a portfolio piece.
avoid_if: You want pay, stability, or hours commensurate with your degree

careers.name: Data Analyst / BI Analyst
careers.summary: Dashboards and SQL-to-insight are exactly what AI agents now do. The most exposed layer of the data stack; move to data engineering (3.6) instead.
careers.degree_note: Use as a stepping stone to data engineering, not a destination.
avoid_if: You want durable demand

careers.name: QA / Test Engineering, IT Support, Sysadmin
careers.summary: BLS projects programmer and support employment to shrink; manual QA is the most automated role in software. Do not aim here with a CS/CE degree.
careers.degree_note: Not a target for a CS/CE graduate.
avoid_if: Always, as a destination

careers.name: Founding a Startup
careers.summary: Extreme variance; better as a second act after a Tier 1 first job that gives you a network, savings, and a real problem to solve.
careers.degree_note: Build in AI/ML or infrastructure first; FDE for customer exposure.
careers.sensitivity: Extreme variance; better as second act
avoid_if: You need income stability
You have not yet worked inside a well-run company
